headline: 700 indie projects reveal default tech stack for 2026, with AI as the new baseline
summary: AI is the most common project tag, freemium models dominate, and TypeScript is nearly caught up with JavaScript in the converged stack.
details: An analysis of 700 public projects and 1,318 builders on the Forg.to platform reveals the emerging trends and the default tech stack for indie hackers by 2026. The study aimed to answer key questions about what founders are actually building.

AI is the single most common project tag, with the entire AI family accounting for 8.5% of all tags. Categories like "AI Agents" and "AI video generation" went from zero to significant numbers in just six months, indicating rapid growth.

Builders are quickly adopting new skills, with LLMs, RAG, LangChain, OpenAI API, and prompt engineering appearing on profiles. This suggests that being "AI-native" is no longer an edge, but rather the expected baseline for new projects.

The analysis shows a quiet convergence on a single, effective setup for indie builders. Product Design, with Figma as the top skill, now outranks Python, highlighting the importance of aesthetics alongside functionality.

TypeScript is rapidly catching up to JavaScript in project tags (49% vs 52%) and is growing faster, making it the clear trend for deep learning. The default kit now includes JavaScript + TypeScript + React + Next.js + Figma + a Postgres backend.

Regarding business models, freemium accounts for 73% of all projects, with free products making up an even larger share. This widespread adoption of a "free-door funnel" has made one-time pricing a potential differentiator.

Despite mobile hype, the platform overwhelmingly shows projects built for the browser. The common strategy is to ship web first, adding mobile support only if user traction demands it, with cross-platform combos being exceptions.

The study also identifies untouched categories, or "whitespace," for indie hackers. These include developer tooling, hardware, and business models that do not start with "free," suggesting opportunities outside crowded areas.

While an AI-enhanced, freemium, web-first SaaS built on the modern stack is a statistically safe bet, it also means fitting into a crowded market. The more interesting move is to apply this stack to underserved niches like testing, hardware, or premium one-time payment products.
